name: ritmillio-tools
description: Cross-agent skills for long-running and unattended engineering work. SKILL.md format, works in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and anything else that reads the open standard.

plugins.name: mattpocock-skills
plugins.description: Passthrough to Matt Pocock's skill pack (grill-me, tdd, to-spec, to-tickets, implement, code-review and friends), installed straight from his repo and kept in sync by /plugin update. Not our code — see https://github.com/mattpocock/skills.

plugins.name: relay
plugins.description: Unattended autonomous work for a stated duration, run as fresh processes handing off a committed ledger. No context rot.

plugins.name: shred-plan
plugins.description: Tear a written plan apart to find gaps before implementing it. Use when the user has a plan (a docs/*-plan.md file or a plan in the conversation) and wants it stress-tested, red-teamed, or 'shredded'. Verifies every codebase claim with evidence, hunts unverified assumptions, hidden dependencies, missing failure modes, scope leaks, and unverifiable done-criteria, then reports findings ranked by severity.

plugins.name: draft-plan
plugins.description: Turn an investigation or conversation into a written plan doc with diagnosis, explicit scope, workstreams with verifiable proofs, sequencing gates, and open questions. Use when the user wants a plan written down before building — then chain into shred-plan to stress-test it.

plugins.name: telegram-notify
plugins.description: Telegram bot notifications for agent events: turn finished, turn failed, commits, pushes, blocked-on-permission, and relay run events. Ships the sender script and walks through BotFather setup, chat id, config, hook wiring and a --doctor check.

plugins.name: reclaim
plugins.description: Diagnose and fix a dev machine pinned at high CPU, high RAM or high load average — read the System-vs-User split first, reap stale build watchers, cap test-runner concurrency, and tell the user when only a reboot will do. Use when the user says the CPU/RAM/fan/load is out of control, shows a system-monitor screenshot, asks to free up memory, or asks why the machine is slow while agents are running.

plugins.name: mac-compromise-check
plugins.description: Run a read-only compromise triage on a macOS machine: accounts, remote access, listening ports, launchd/cron persistence, browser extensions, MDM/config profiles, and system hardening (FileVault/SIP/Gatekeeper). Trace a specific email or account across the machine. Use when the user says 'is my Mac hacked', 'check if my Mac is compromised', 'did someone access my machine', shows a suspicious sign-in, or wants a security audit of their laptop.

plugins.name: collect-bills
plugins.description: Sweep mailboxes for vendor invoices billed to the company, drop anything without the company tax number, diff against what is already archived, and download only the delta. Use when the user says collect the bills, gather receipts, get the invoices, or do the bookkeeping.

plugins.name: safe-migration
plugins.description: Run the safe Drizzle migration ritual for a repo with a fragile migration directory: pick the next free prefix, generate, grep the SQL for destructive operations, enforce IF EXISTS, run the migration check, and confirm schema lands with its migration in one commit. Use when the user changes a Drizzle schema file, says 'generate a migration', 'add a column/table', 'db:generate', or is about to ship a schema change.

plugins.name: vercel-triage
plugins.description: Pull, dedupe, and triage Vercel production logs down to genuine failures, working around the CLI's traps (events duplicated many times, short --until windows, ~24h retention). Use when the user says 'check the vercel logs', 'is prod erroring', 'triage production', 'why are users seeing errors', or wants a production health read.

plugins.name: morning-brief
plugins.description: Produce a one-screen morning brief: an INTERNAL section (git activity, open PRs, and relay ledgers across the user's repos) and an EXTERNAL section (news pulled from sources listed in a config file), optionally delivered to Telegram. Use when the user says 'morning brief', 'daily digest', 'catch me up', 'what happened overnight', 'get the news', or wants a start-of-day summary without browsing.
